transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Hello! I'm Dora, your clinical conversational agent. I've reviewed your post-cataract surgery follow-up check, and I'm here to answer any questions you may have about your recovery. Do you have any questions about your surgery or recovery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Hi, thanks for speaking with me. I do have a few questions. First, when can I start doing a little bit of gardening?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: After cataract surgery, it's generally recommended to avoid strenuous exercise, including heavy lifting and bending, for about a month. However, you can start with light exercise, such as brisk walking, gardening, or gentle cycling, about 1 week after surgery. Just be sure to wear protective eyewear when gardening, and take regular breaks to rest your eyes. Does that sound okay to you? Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: That sounds good, thank you. My next question is, when can I start using my eye gel for dry eyes?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You should continue to use your eye drops as prescribed. If you're running out, your GP should be able to provide some more. And if you were using any eye drops before your operation, such as for dry eyes, it's safe to continue using them, unless you've been told otherwise. Just make sure to follow the instructions on the bottle and ask your GP if you have any questions. Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thank you for clarifying that. I do have another question — I'm very sensitive to bright light. Is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: It's normal for your eyes to be sensitive to light as they adjust to the new lenses. If it's mild and just seems brighter than usual, wearing sunglasses when you're outside might help. But if it's severe and you're also experiencing redness or pain, we may need to take a closer look. Does that sound like your situation? Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: That makes sense, thanks for explaining. I have one last question — should I still have some blurriness by now?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: It's common to have blurry vision for a little while after cataract surgery, especially in the first week or so. But if your vision is still blurry or getting significantly worse, we may need to check it to make sure everything is okay. It's also possible that you'll need reading glasses or varifocals for reading, as the standard lens we put in is usually for distance vision. Would you like to know more about that?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: No, that's clear, thank you. I appreciate all your help. I don't have any more questions at the moment.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: It was my pleasure to help. I'm glad we could clear up any concerns you had. Before we go, can you confirm that all your questions about your cataract surgery recovery have been answered?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, all my questions have been answered. Thank you for your assistance!
